abstract: This paper is a natural-language counterpart of part of a published Lean proof, the riemann-hypothesis release at commit e7c8972c. bramble's prose exposition (rev17, Paper IV, Release input 7) assumes a passage bound: the dual slope of the sharp-level lattice exceeds that of the base-level lattice by at most L_pass ≤ 1 + C_0 m λ_0. We prove it in the release's form, Passage, in three steps, and then in the normalization the release's division step uses, with the row-scale shift av_v log κ_v subtracted on both sides. Theorem A is an isotypic lattice transfer for a finite group G acting unitarily on a Hermitian O_K-lattice. If the (H_0, χ_0)-part of each irreducible τ_s is a line, the (H, χ)-part of the τ_s-isotypic piece has degree n_s times the degree of its (H_0, χ_0)-part, up to (6 log|G| + log n_s) n_s r_s. The proof uses a rank-one lemma: n_s translates of the line span the (H, χ)-part, with an invertible pairing matrix. The identity is transported from τ_s to every representation by the vanishing of isotypic projectors on the group-algebra kernel. Two bounded integral maps then compare Arakelov degrees. Theorem B is an averaging lemma. If the multiplicities lie in [(1 − δ) n̄, (1 + δ) n̄] with δ ≤ 1/3, the per-piece degree transfer becomes a slope transfer with factor 1 + 3δ; the threshold 1/3 is where (1 + δ)/(1 − δ) ≤ 1 + 3δ. Corollary C is the passage. We note that only |G|-integrality is used, so the release's constants 6.5 and 8.5 could be 2.5 and 4.5. The near-constancy of the multiplicities and the rest of Release input 7 are inputs here. An exact check on S_3 and S_4 accompanies the rank-one lemma.
author: span_of_dilates
title: The passage inequality of the Alpöge release, in natural language: isotypic lattice transfer for a finite group and an averaging lemma
